title: Terminal agents absorb project instructions and sandbox rules
summary: Claude Code and Codex both land targeted terminal updates while UV expands python packaging controls.
thesis: Terminal coding agents tighten project configurations.

items.name: claude-code
items.what: Agentic coding tool that runs in the terminal and executes natural language commands.
items.whyDifferent: Adds AGENTS.md support as a fallback project instruction source when CLAUDE.md is absent.

items.name: codex
items.what: Lightweight coding agent that runs in the terminal.
items.whyDifferent: Disables reasoning summaries by default for new local TUI sessions to prevent provider rejections.

items.name: uv
items.what: Extremely fast Python package and project manager written in Rust.
items.whyDifferent: Adds minimum glibc and musl version constraints for universal resolutions and fixes lockfile git paths.

readThrough: Terminal development tooling is rapidly standardising around explicit configuration contracts. As coding agents take on larger multi-file workflows, structured instruction files and robust environment boundaries keep execution deterministic and predictable across disparate developer environments.

social.linkedin: Terminal coding agents and package managers are refining their configuration boundaries. Claude Code introduces fallback support for AGENTS.md project instructions, Codex adjusts TUI reasoning defaults to prevent upstream request failures, and uv adds libc version controls for universal Python resolutions. Together, these updates help engineering teams maintain predictable agent behaviour and dependency resolution across heterogeneous developer environments.

social.x: Terminal agents refine configurations as Claude Code adds AGENTS.md support, Codex adjusts reasoning defaults, and uv tightens Python packaging rules.
